title: Bioinformatics for Healthcare Quality Management: Clinical Outcomes, Implementation Barriers, and Care Improvement.
titlePt: Bioinformatics for Healthcare Quality Management: Clinical Outcomes, Implementation Barriers, and Care Improvement.
abstract: The bioinformatics-enabled workflows as quality-management tools have become central to modern healthcare, enabling genomic sequencing, transcriptomics, proteomics, and multiomics integration to support clinical decision-making. Despite expanding adoption, synthesized evidence on measurable clinical value and organizational, workforce, interoperability, governance, and equity barriers remains limited. To synthesize evidence on the contribution of bioinformatics-enabled workflows to healthcare quality improvement, care-process performance, clinical decision-making, patient outcomes, and implementation challenges from 2015 to 2025. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and IEEE Xplore. title: HDL-C Levels Are Associated with Clinical Outcomes and Hospital Mortality in Critically Ill Patients with Sepsis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
titlePt: HDL-C Levels Are Associated with Clinical Outcomes and Hospital Mortality in Critically Ill Patients with Sepsis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Metabolic perturbations frequently occur during the acute phase of critical illness and may disrupt lipid homeostasis. Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a severe condition and is associated with high mortality in critically ill patients with sepsis. This study aimed to evaluate the association between conventional plasma lipid parameters and clinical outcomes in critically ill sepsis patients. Materials and Methods: We conducted a prospective observational cohort study of critically ill sepsis patients in Taiwan between October 2020 and July 2025. Conventional plasma lipid parameters and clinical variables were measured at intensive care unit admission. Clinical outcomes were compared between patients stratified by plasma HDL-C levels. title: Duration of effectiveness of tuberculosis preventive treatment across various tuberculosis burden settings: a systematic review and individual-participant meta-analysis.
titlePt: Duration of effectiveness of tuberculosis preventive treatment across various tuberculosis burden settings: a systematic review and individual-participant meta-analysis.
abstract: Millions of individuals at risk of tuberculosis are given tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT) annually. However, questions remain regarding the duration of protection from TPT and potential variability across populations and settings with disparate tuberculosis risk. We aimed to assess the effect of TPT on time to tuberculosis among close contacts of individuals with tuberculosis and with evidence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection across high-burden, medium-burden, and low-burden settings. In this systematic review and individual-participant meta-analysis, we searched MEDLINE, PubMed, Web of Science, BIOSIS, and Embase for cohort studies and randomised controlled trials published between Jan 1, 1998, and Aug 28, 2023. abstract: To evaluate how confounding by indication and notoriety bias shape the apparent semaglutide-panic attack signal in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and to interpret this signal using an evidence-triangulation framework integrating randomized and observational studies. title: Association of Recurrence-free Interval With Survival After Recurrence in Gastric Cancer: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
titlePt: Association of Recurrence-free Interval With Survival After Recurrence in Gastric Cancer: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
abstract: The prognostic significance of recurrence-free interval (RFI) after gastrectomy in patients with gastric cancer (GC) remains unclear, and previous studies have reported inconsistent associations between the timing of recurrence and survival after recurrence. This study evaluated the association of RFI with post-recurrence overall survival (OS) and recurrence patterns in patients receiving first-line chemotherapy for recurrent GC. This multicenter retrospective study included 190 patients who underwent R0 gastrectomy and subsequently received first-line chemotherapy for recurrence between January 2015 and September 2025. RFI was analyzed as a log-transformed continuous variable and its association with post-recurrence OS was evaluated using multivariable Cox regression and restricted cubic spline models. title: Functional Health Illiteracy in Cancer Patients and Caregivers in the Era of Precision Medicine and Immunotherapy: A Narrative Review.
titlePt: Functional Health Illiteracy in Cancer Patients and Caregivers in the Era of Precision Medicine and Immunotherapy: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Functional health illiteracy is a significant barrier to equitable cancer care for patients and caregivers, a challenge that is exacerbated by precision medicine and immunotherapy. This review article aimed at synthesizing current evidence on functional health illiteracy among cancer patients and caregivers and examines its interaction with the demands of precision medicine and immunotherapy. The article also outlines practical strategies to mitigate the impact of health illiteracy on therapy adherence, decision-making, and clinical outcomes. Articles published between 2010 and 2025 were identified through searches of PubMed, CINAHL, and PsycINFO. abstract: Background/Objectives: Longitudinal monitoring after CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy primarily focuses on CAR-T-cell expansion. title: Comparative risk assessment of cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes using cystatin C and creatinine in DECLARE-TIMI 58.
titlePt: Comparative risk assessment of cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes using cystatin C and creatinine in DECLARE-TIMI 58.
abstract: The relationship between cystatin C and cardiovascular and kidney outcomes is not well explored in individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and normal or mild kidney dysfunction. This nested prospective biomarker study included patients enrolled in DECLARE-TIMI 58. Participants were categorized into quartiles of CysC/creatinine and eGFRCysC/eGFRCr and classified according to Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) risk categories. Hazard ratios were estimated for a composite of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure (CVD/HHF), major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and a kidney-specific composite outcome (persistent ≥40% decrease in eGFR, end-stage renal disease, or renal death). Among 1899 placebo-treated patients, higher baseline CysC was associated with higher risk for CVD/HHF, MACE, and the kidney-specific composite outcome. title: Cold plasma technology as a novel antimicrobial platform: mechanisms, efficacy, and clinical translation: a systematic literature review.
titlePt: Cold plasma technology as a novel antimicrobial platform: mechanisms, efficacy, and clinical translation: a systematic literature review.
abstract: The global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) crisis necessitates innovative therapeutic approaches beyond traditional antibiotics. Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP), an ionized gas containing reactive species, has emerged as a potent physical antimicrobial technology with broad-spectrum activity. This systematic review critically evaluates current evidence on CAP's antimicrobial mechanisms, efficacy against diverse pathogens, and clinical translation potential. We conducted a systematic literature search following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases (January 2018-December 2025). abstract: Background: Procalcitonin (PCT) may support decision-making in abdominal and emergency surgery when infection is difficult to distinguish from non-infectious inflammation. Its interpretation remains challenging because clinical settings, sampling schedules, and proposed thresholds vary. title: Procalcitonin in Acute Pancreatitis: Diagnostic Utility for Differentiating Infected from Sterile Pancreatic Necrosis.
titlePt: Procalcitonin in Acute Pancreatitis: Diagnostic Utility for Differentiating Infected from Sterile Pancreatic Necrosis.
abstract: Acute pancreatitis (AP) is an acute inflammatory disorder of the pancreas that disrupts its normal function and often requires hospitalization because of severe abdominal pain. While most patients recover without major complications, some develop pancreatic necrosis, infected pancreatic necrosis (IPN), persistent organ failure, and other severe complications associated with increased morbidity and mortality. A key clinical challenge is distinguishing infected pancreatic necrosis from sterile pancreatic inflammation, as delayed or inaccurate diagnosis may result in inappropriate antibiotic use and poorer clinical outcomes. This review aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic utility of procalcitonin (PCT) in differentiating infected pancreatic necrosis from sterile inflammation and to assess its role in supporting antimicrobial decision-making in patients with AP. abstract: ObjectiveTo characterize the burden of herpes zoster (HZ) in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and to examine clinical correlates of HZ and patients' attitudes toward the recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV).MethodsWe conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study combined with a cross-sectional survey among consecutive adult outpatients with SLE between December 2024 and June 2025. abstract: To our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival. This open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. title: Mechanisms of Traditional Chinese Medicine-Derived Active Components in the Treatment of Alzheimer's Disease: A Comprehensive Review.
titlePt: Mechanisms of Traditional Chinese Medicine-Derived Active Components in the Treatment of Alzheimer's Disease: A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline and multifactorial pathology. Because AD involves interacting pathological processes, the limited efficacy of conventional single-target therapies has increased interest in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and other natural medicines with multi-target pharmacological actions. TCM-derived active components originate from medicinal materials used in traditional practice and are evaluated using modern pharmacological approaches. Their source medicines have diverse traditional-use backgrounds. Some have historical associations with memory or cognitive symptoms, whereas many others were traditionally used for broader deficiency, phlegm, blood-stasis, heat, or related syndromic patterns. title: Monocarboxylate transporters in physiology and cancer: from fundamentals to clinical translation.
titlePt: Monocarboxylate transporters in physiology and cancer: from fundamentals to clinical translation.
abstract: Monocarboxylate transporters (MCTs) are vital to physiological pH regulation, redox balance, and energy homeostasis, as they mediate proton-coupled transport of lactate and other monocarboxylates across cell membranes. MCT1 and MCT4 are especially important during metabolically demanding states, where they support lactate shuttling between oxidative and glycolytic cells. To sustain rapid growth and biosynthesis, the metabolism of highly proliferative cells, including cancer cells, shifts toward glycolysis with increased lactate production. In this setting, MCTs enable lactate and proton efflux, preventing intracellular acidification and maintaining glycolytic flux. Cancer cells frequently co-opt this system, overexpressing MCT1 and MCT4, which is associated with aggressive behavior, poor prognosis, and treatment resistance. abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained arrhythmia in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), occurring in 20-25% of patients and associated with increased morbidity, stroke risk, and symptom burden. Despite this substantial clinical impact, the understanding of the short-term natural history of AF, including recurrence and the effectiveness of treatment strategies in HCM, remains poorly characterized. We assessed 2016 patients referred to Lahey Hospital and Medical Center for the diagnosis and subspecialty management of HCM, of whom 341 (17%) had a remote history of AF (≥5 years), and 149 (7%) had AF episodes initially detected between January 2020 and June 2025. These 149 patients were included in this retrospective analysis to allow comprehensive short-term assessment of AF recurrence, treatment interventions, and clinical outcomes from first detected AF utilizing contemporary treatments. title: Current Evidence on Periprocedural Flat-Panel CT in Endovascular Stroke Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract: Periprocedural flat-panel computed tomography (FPCT) may complement real-time decision-making during endovascular treatment for stroke. This study aims to summarize current evidence on diagnostic findings, prognostic associations, and clinical applications of periprocedural FPCT in the angiography suite. Medline, Embase, and Scopus were searched for studies published between January 2019 and September 2025 reporting on periprocedural FPCT in endovascular treatment patients (noncontrast FPCT, 3-dimensional-digital subtraction angiography/contrast-enhanced FPCT, or FPCT perfusion). titlePt: High-Resolution Disconnectome Predicts Outcome and Response to Thrombectomy in Basilar Artery Occlusion.
abstract: Acute basilar artery occlusion causes devastating strokes. Despite the benefit of endovascular treatment, the optimal management remains controversial in specific subgroups, particularly patients with mild deficits, and would benefit from robust prognostic tools. Given the dense white matter networks within the posterior fossa, we tested whether quantifying disconnections from acute diffusion-weighted imaging could improve outcome prediction and identify responders to recanalization compared with conventional metrics. We conducted a secondary analysis of a prospective multicenter stroke registry in France, including consecutive patients (2017-2024) with basilar artery occlusion and admission magnetic resonance imaging. titlePt: A novel spliceosome inhibitor triggers anti-tumor CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses in murine models of pediatric-relevant cancer.
abstract: Immunotherapy has been proved to have a high potential to change the outcomes of patients with advanced cancer. However, the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in most classical pediatric cancers remains limited, underscoring the need for other novel immunomodulatory strategies, such as small-molecule agents, either synthetically derived or isolated from natural sources, which can modulate intracellular immune pathways. Among these, spliceosome inhibitors have emerged as a promising class of compounds capable of reshaping the tumor antigenic landscape. We developed a new generation of spliceosome-targeting molecules that interfere with mRNA processing, enhance major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) and MHC-II expression in tumor cell, and potentiate T cell-mediated immune responses. title: Neurobiology of exercise in Parkinson's disease.
titlePt: Neurobiology of exercise in Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Epidemiological, preclinical, and clinical studies increasingly support exercise as a potent neuroprotective and disease-modifying intervention in Parkinson's disease (PD). Preclinical studies, including toxin- and α-synuclein-based models, using voluntary, forced, and skilled exercise paradigms demonstrate preservation of nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons, improved motor function, and activation of convergent pathways. Protective processes include upregulation of neurotrophic factors (BDNF, GDNF, VEGF and Irisin), enhanced mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative resilience, reduced neuroinflammation, improved basal ganglia synaptic plasticity and increased lysosomal functions. Additional emerging mechanisms underlying exercise-induced neuroprotection involve vascular remodeling, pathways regulating cellular oxygen and hypoxia, modulation of the gut microbiome, and epigenetic reprogramming. title: Epidemiology and antimicrobial susceptibility of Vibrio cholerae in recurrent cholera outbreaks in Ethiopia: a multicenter study.
titlePt: Epidemiology and antimicrobial susceptibility of Vibrio cholerae in recurrent cholera outbreaks in Ethiopia: a multicenter study.
abstract: The recurrence of cholera continues to be a public health concern in Ethiopia. The emergence of antimicrobial-resistant Vibrio cholerae strains has complicated case management. Thus, this study aimed to assess the epidemiologic distribution and antimicrobial susceptibility profile of V. cholerae in Ethiopia. A cross-sectional study was conducted among patients in cholera treatment centers and health care facilities in Ethiopia from September 2023 to September 2025. Diarrheic stool and suspected water samples were collected and transported to the Ethiopian Public Health Institute to isolate and confirm V. cholerae using standard microbiology techniques. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed by the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion and E-test methods in accordance with updated Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute guidelines. abstract: Nutraceuticals and phytoceuticals are increasingly investigated for bipolar disorder (BD). We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, PsycINFO, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to July 1, 2025. Co-primary outcomes were changes in depressive or manic symptoms (standardized mean difference [SMD]), treatment response, and acceptability (risk ratio [RR]); tolerability and remission (RR) were secondary outcomes. Heterogeneity, transitivity, inconsistency, small-study effects, risk of bias, and confidence in evidence (CINeMA) were assessed. Twenty-eight RCTs (n=2,222) evaluated 22 treatments. titlePt: Prunella Oral Liquid in combination with Western medical treatment for Graves' disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Prunella Oral Liquid is a Chinese patent medicine prepared from Prunella vulgaris L. Modern pharmacological studies indicate that its primary active constituents, such as rosmarinic acid, possess significant anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and antioxidant properties. Although it is widely used in clinical practice for Graves' disease (GD), uncertainty remains. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Prunella Oral Liquid in patients with GD. We searched seven databases for the randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of Prunella Oral Liquid on GD patients from inception to September 2025, and references in the literature were hand searched. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 1.0. Data analysis was performed using RevMan 5.4. The certainty of evidence was evaluated with the GRADE framework. title: Tau isoform mapping across tissues and biofluids reveals a signature distinguishing Alzheimer's disease from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
titlePt: Tau isoform mapping across tissues and biofluids reveals a signature distinguishing Alzheimer's disease from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
abstract: Blood phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) accurately detects Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology but is also elevated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), likely reflecting peripheral (big) tau released from muscle. Assays selectively measuring brain-derived (BD-) tau and BD-p-tau217 are therefore needed. We analysed serum BD-tau and p-tau217 in ALS (n = 139), AD (n = 101) and controls (n = 75) using direct immunoassays and after BD-Tau immunoprecipitation (BD-Tau-IP), and tau species in brain (n = 16), spinal cord (n = 11) and muscle (n = 10) by targeted mass spectrometry. With the direct immunoassays, BD-tau and p-tau217 were increased in AD and ALS versus controls. After BD-Tau-IP, BD-tau and BD-p-tau217 were elevated in AD only, improving diagnostic accuracy. abstract: Molecular profiling of ovarian cancer is feasible and provides valuable therapeutic and research information to women in Aotearoa New Zealand. Sixteen women consecutively diagnosed with apparent advanced ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer underwent molecular profiling as part of INOVATe (Individualised Ovarian Cancer Treatment through Integration of Genomic Pathology into Multidisciplinary Care), an ovarian cancer precision medicine programme conducted in New South Wales, Australia. All eligible women who were approached agreed to participate in the study. Molecular profiling was successfully undertaken on tumour tissue samples stored after primary surgery and in two of three core biopsy samples. title: Biomarkers and future directions for immunotherapy in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer: a systematic review.
titlePt: Biomarkers and future directions for immunotherapy in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer: a systematic review.
abstract: The mechanisms of resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC) have 3 interconnected levels, which provide information to guide different biomarker strategies. There is a critical clinical need, as objective response rates continue to be < 10%. We suggest a biomarker stratification model on the basis of clinical actionability. title: Discovery of 4-Aminoquinazoline Derivatives as Potent PKMYT1 Inhibitors via Hydrogen Bond Donor-To-Acceptor Conversion for CCNE1-Amplified Cancers.
titlePt: Discovery of 4-Aminoquinazoline Derivatives as Potent PKMYT1 Inhibitors via Hydrogen Bond Donor-To-Acceptor Conversion for CCNE1-Amplified Cancers.
abstract: PKMYT1 is a critical regulator of the cell cycle and has emerged as a promising synthetic lethal target for CCNE1-amplified cancers. In this study, we report the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of a novel series of 4-aminoquinazoline-based PKMYT1 inhibitors. A hydrogen bond donor-to-acceptor conversion strategy was successfully employed to reduce the hydrogen bond donor (HBD) count, thereby improving the drug-likeness of this series. Among them, compound 12f exhibited nanomolar inhibitory activity against PKMYT1 and potent antiproliferative activity in the OVCAR-3 ovarian cancer cell line. Furthermore, compound 12f demonstrated synergistic antiproliferative effects when combined with PARP inhibitors. Along with an acceptable oral pharmacokinetic profile, compound 12f demonstrated robust in vivo efficacy in OVCAR-3 xenograft models. title: Bridging drug labels and precision medicine: pharmacogenomic opportunities in recent US-FDA drug approvals.
titlePt: Bridging drug labels and precision medicine: pharmacogenomic opportunities in recent US-FDA drug approvals.
abstract: Pharmacogenomics (PGx) information in US-FDA drug labels supports precision prescribing. This study aimed to quantify the proportion of recent US-FDA-approved drug labels containing PGx information, identify additional drugs with potential PGx relevance through mechanistic pathway analysis, and assess the availability of US-FDA-approved companion diagnostic tests. Novel systemic drugs approved by the US-FDA between 1 January 2021 and 31 December 2025 were identified. Drug labels were evaluated using the FDA Table of Pharmacogenomic Biomarkers in Drug Labeling. Drugs without labeled PGx information were assessed for potential PGx relevance through evaluation of metabolic enzymes and transporter pathways using CPIC, DPWG, and PharmGKB. titlePt: From etiology to precision oncology: a systematic review of the causes and evolving treatments of prostate cancer.
abstract: Prostate cancer remains one of the most frequently diagnosed malignancies and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among men globally. Its development is driven by a complex interaction of genetic susceptibility, molecular alterations, hormonal signaling, environmental exposures, and lifestyle-related factors. This systematic review synthesizes current evidence on the etiological mechanisms and evolving therapeutic landscape of prostate cancer. A systematic review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Literature published between January 2010 and December 2025 was searched in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases. titlePt: Early Rhythm Control vs Usual Care After Acute Ischemic Stroke in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.
abstract: Early rhythm control reduces cardiovascular events in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF); however, its effectiveness in the setting of acute ischemic stroke remains uncertain. We aimed to examine whether early rhythm control after acute ischemic stroke is associated with a lower risk of recurrent stroke or systemic embolism (SE) in patients with AF. This nationwide cohort study used the DeSC-IQVIA integrated database, an administrative claims database covering approximately 16 million individuals in Japan. Adults hospitalized for acute ischemic stroke with AF present at admission between 2014 and 2025 were included. title: Weight loss and blood pressure lowering with GLP-1 receptor agonists and multi-hormone receptor modulators in overweight and obesity: a systematic review and meta-regression of phase 3 clinical trials.
titlePt: Weight loss and blood pressure lowering with GLP-1 receptor agonists and multi-hormone receptor modulators in overweight and obesity: a systematic review and meta-regression of phase 3 clinical trials.
abstract: Obesity and hypertension frequently coexist, and weight-reduction is recommended as a core strategy for blood pressure (BP) management in adults with overweight or obesity. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and emerging multi-hormone receptor modulators (MHRMs) induce substantial weight loss alongside modest BP reductions. However, the extent to which weight-loss is associated with BP lowering across these therapies remains unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of phase 3 randomized controlled trials evaluating GLP-1RAs and MHRMs in adults with overweight or obesity (PROSPERO: CRD420251146441). We searched Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid Embase, the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from 1946 to December 2025. abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) is the leading global cause of death from a single infectious agent. Recent reductions in global health funding have threatened TB control, making comprehensive assessment of TB, HIV-related TB, and drug-resistant TB burdens before these disruptions essential for shaping effective responses. abstract: This study aimed to evaluate physicians' preparedness to manage juvenile obesity (JO) in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region by assessing their attitudes, knowledge, clinical practices, confidence, and perceived barriers. A 38-question cross-sectional survey was created, validated, and distributed in December 2024 across MENA countries using a skip-logic-tailored, bilingual (Arabic/English) online platform. It assessed physicians' attitudes, familiarity with JO-management guidelines and concepts, screening and treatment practices, prior JO-training, confidence, and barriers. Data were analyzed using both descriptive and inferential statistics. The study included 400 physicians (54% female, 57% younger than 35, 65% primary care physicians). 90% considered JO a routine checkup priority. abstract: Despite evidence supporting methadone analgesic efficacy, perioperative methadone use remains limited due to concerns regarding respiratory depression. title: Prevalence and spectrum of variants in homologous recombination repair genes in ovarian cancer in Latin America: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
titlePt: Prevalence and spectrum of variants in homologous recombination repair genes in ovarian cancer in Latin America: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Ovarian cancer is a major cause of gynecologic cancer mortality worldwide, with disproportionately poor outcomes in Latin America (LATAM). Variants in homologous recombination repair genes, especially BRCA1/2, are predictive biomarkers for platinum-based chemotherapy and PARP inhibitors. However, data on the prevalence and spectrum of homologous recombination repair variants in LATAM populations remain limited. To synthesize the prevalence and spectrum of pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants in homologous recombination repair pathway genes among LATAM ovarian cancer patients and highlight clinical and research implications. The review protocol was developed in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) and was registered in the international prospective register of systematic reviews (PROSPERO; registration number CRD420251019706). abstract: Over the past decade, phytotherapy such as licorice has attracted research as an alternative to antibiotic growth promoters in broiler production, driven by rising concerns over antimicrobial resistance. titlePt: Continuous oximetry monitoring in children admitted after adenotonsillectomy, an observational study.
abstract: Children undergoing adenotonsillectomy (AT) are frequently admitted overnight because of concerns regarding postoperative respiratory events. The current admission guidelines are largely based on retrospective data. Continuous overnight oximetry may better define the incidence and severity of clinically meaningful postoperative desaturation. We sought to determine the incidence of significant overnight oxygen desaturation (SpO2 <85% for >30 s) or supplemental oxygen requirement in non-syndromic children admitted for AT. This prospective observational study was conducted at the Texas Children's Hospital, a tertiary freestanding pediatric hospital. Consecutive patients admitted following AT between July 26, 2024, and May 27, 2025, were assessed for eligibility. Patients with fewer than 4 h of overnight oximetry data were excluded. abstract: Autoimmune diseases are a heterogeneous group of chronic diseases characterised by loss of immune tolerance with substantial morbidity and mortality. Since 2021, chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells have recently emerged as a promising treatment option for patients with severe, refractory autoimmune diseases. abstract: Relapsed or refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (R/R B-ALL) patients exhibit heterogeneous responses to CD19 chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy. abstract: Severe mental illness (SMI) often limits participation in traditional therapy due to motivational and cognitive deficits. We examined short-term clinical changes during use of a personalized video-based mobile app (MARO)-providing psychoeducation, emotion regulation, cognitive restructuring, and behavioral activation-in community-dwelling individuals with SMI and explored whether the timing of minimal human coaching was associated with these outcomes. abstract: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) have demonstrated neuroprotective effects in preclinical models of Parkinson's disease (PD), but individual ARBs differ in pharmacological properties that may influence their neuroprotective potential. abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, with the highest burden in the first 6 months of life. Maternal immunization with the bivalent (RSV-A and RSV-B) prefusion F (RSVPreF) protein subunit vaccine (ABRYSVO) is a recently recommended strategy for preventing RSV-related outcomes in infants. titlePt: Split intein-mediated reconstitution of regulatable CAR T-cells.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has transformed the treatment of B-cell malignancies. However, strategies that improve the modularity and controllability of CAR signaling could broaden its applicability and safety across additional clinical contexts. abstract: Brain-derived phosphorylated tau species are postulated to improve the detection of Alzheimer's disease pathology by mitigating non-specific increases. abstract: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) is a progressive disease associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. abstract: Biologic and immunomodulatory agents now account for roughly one-third of annual FDA drug approvals and are rapidly migrating from specialty clinics into community, ambulatory, and primary-care settings. abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are important therapeutic options for obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Despite their increasing use, safety concerns remain, and pharmacy students' knowledge of their adverse effects is unclear. title: Dysregulation of glycogen metabolism in cardiomyopathy caused by glycogenin-1 (GYG1) missense variants.
titlePt: Dysregulation of glycogen metabolism in cardiomyopathy caused by glycogenin-1 (GYG1) missense variants.
abstract: Glycogen storage diseases are inherited disorders of glycogen metabolism and are commonly associated with hypoglycemia, hepatic dysfunction, or skeletal and cardiac myopathy, depending on the affected enzyme. Glycogen storage disease type 15 (GSD15) is caused by pathogenic variants in GYG1, which encodes glycogenin-1, the autoglucosylating primer required for glycogen synthesis. GSD15 is characterized by cardiomyopathy and storage of abnormal glycogen and polyglucosan in cardiomyocytes. To understand the pathobiology of GSD15, we investigated the storage material in heart explants from 2 previously reported patients and described a new case of GSD15. abstract: Esophageal mucosal injury and gastroparesis are clinically important complications of radiofrequency ablation (RFA) of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) is a non-thermal modality that may spare these complications due to its myocardial tissue selectivity. We aimed to compare the incidence of endoscopically detected esophageal lesions (EDELs) and suspected gastroparesis between RFA and PFA as the primary endpoints. abstract: This systematic review synthesized existing research about associations between sidewalk availability and quality and children's physical health outcomes. Google Scholar, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched. The initial search strategy was intentionally broad, encompassing all age groups and physical health outcomes in relation to sidewalk access, quality, and connectivity. One hundred and eighty-four eligible studies were identified among 17,726; the retained studies were categorized by age group. This review focuses on 39 articles that specifically examined associations between sidewalk infrastructure and physical health outcomes in children. abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a common cardiovascular complication of diabetes. Early identification of unrecognized HF enables initiation of disease-modifying therapies. International diabetes and HF clinical practice guidelines are inconsistent with respect to recommendations for screening for HF in people with diabetes. Community-based participants aged ≥40 years with type 1 or type 2 diabetes and at least 1 additional HF risk factor, but without known HF, were recruited in the west of Scotland. title: Fatty liver and adipokines: converging pathways linking insulin resistance to early atherosclerosis in obese children and adolescents.
titlePt: Fatty liver and adipokines: converging pathways linking insulin resistance to early atherosclerosis in obese children and adolescents.
abstract: Childhood obesity drives nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and adipokine dysregulation, converging on insulin resistance (IR) to promote subclinical vascular injury measurable as increased carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT). Pediatric-specific mechanistic integration of these pathways with early atherosclerosis remains incompletely characterized. This review synthesizes evidence on NAFLD severity and cIMT in obese youth, examines the roles of resistin, high-molecular-weight (HMW) adiponectin, chemerin, and inflammatory mediators in IR-driven vascular remodeling, and evaluates their diagnostic and therapeutic implications. A structured narrative review following SANRA guidance was conducted. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from January 2000 to March 2025 for studies enrolling children aged 2-18 years with obesity and reporting cIMT measured by B-mode ultrasonography alongside NAFLD or adipokine measures. titlePt: Potential links between PCOS/PMOS and Alzheimer disease and related dementias.
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome/polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PCOS/PMOS) is a common endocrine disorder with significant metabolic and reproductive implications. Increasing attention has focused on its potential long-term neurological consequences, including possible links to cognitive impairment and Alzheimer disease (AD), through overlapping biological pathways. We conducted a comprehensive PubMed search, from inception through October 2025, identifying studies on cognitive performance, brain structure and function, neurodegenerative biomarkers, and dementia risk in PCOS/PMOS patients. Evidence supports multiple potential mechanistic pathways that could connect PCOS/PMOS to AD-relevant biology, such as insulin resistance (IR), chronic inflammation, hormonal dysregulation, and cardiovascular dysfunction. abstract: The variable-loop circular catheter (VLCC, VARIPULSE) is a pulsed-field ablation (PFA) catheter equipped with a Tissue Proximity Indication (TPI) function, which monitors catheter-tissue contact. abstract: Neonatal septic shock represents a life-threatening complication of neonatal sepsis associated with substantial in-hospital mortality. abstract: Pediatric overweight and obesity (OW/OB) is a major public health concern associated with significant short- and long-term health risks. title: Proteomic dysregulation associated with cerebral amyloid angiopathy.
titlePt: Proteomic dysregulation associated with cerebral amyloid angiopathy.
abstract: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) is characterized by impaired vascular amyloid-β clearance, distinct from Alzheimer's disease (AD), underscoring the need to clarify its molecular basis for predicting therapy-related amyloid-related imaging abnormalities. We analyzed post-mortem brain proteomics from Religious Orders Study and Rush Memory and Aging Project (ROS/MAP) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteomics from Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) to identify CAA-associated proteins and network modules, delineate their biological processes and cellular origins, and determine their diagnostic performance. Proteomics analysis identified 30 proteins as associated with CAA severity, enriched in pathways distinct from AD pathology, with 11 replicated in ADNI. Two CAA-associated modules were enriched for microglial vesicle transport and astrocytic potassium-ion homeostasis. abstract: Obesity substantially influences clinical and metabolic manifestations of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). However, differences in clinical, metabolic, and hormonal profiles between obese and lean women with PCOS have not been explored in large-scale meta-analyses. abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of non-pharmacological interventions in improving MetS-related metabolic-control outcomes among adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. title: Ulcerated infantile hemangioma in the β-blocker era: recent advances.
titlePt: Ulcerated infantile hemangioma in the β-blocker era: recent advances.
abstract: Whilst β-blockers have revolutionized the management of complicated infantile hemangiomas (IHs), ulceration remains a highly painful and clinically challenging complication. Ulcerated IHs may lead to pain, bleeding, secondary infection, feeding or diaper-care difficulties, functional impairment, and permanent scarring. Early recognition and integrated management are therefore essential. This narrative review searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases from inception to June 2026 for studies concerning ulcerated IH. The search was restricted to publications written in English; relevant evidence was synthesized in a narrative fashion. Ulceration is more likely to occur in rapidly proliferating, large, superficial, mixed, segmental, or partially segmental IHs. This is particularly so for those involving the lips, neck, diaper area, perineal or anogenital region, and skin folds. Early white discoloration is an important warning sign of impending ulceration. abstract: Pulsed field ablation is now widely used for atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation, but atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence remains common and postablation risk tools are limited. abstract: With the acceleration of global population aging, early diagnosis and intervention of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and other neurodegenerative disorders have become major public health challenges. Olfactory dysfunction (OD) is increasingly recognized as one of the earliest clinical manifestations of AD, highlighting the importance of understanding the relationship between AD and olfactory impairment. This study integrates bibliometric analysis and genomic approaches to systematically characterize global research trends and explore potential molecular mechanisms underlying AD and OD from 2006 to 2025. abstract: Cardiorenal evidence for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) derives mainly from trials in overweight or obesity; data in adults with Type 2 diabetes (T2D) and body mass index (BMI) below 27 kg/m2 are limited. We emulated a target trial in the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (index dates 2020 to 2026; maximum follow-up 24 months). Adults with T2D and BMI < 27 kg/m2 newly initiating non-tirzepatide GLP-1 RAs were compared with new users of dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4i), sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) or usual care. titlePt: Questionable Evidence for Berberine in Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome: An Integrity-Based Reappraisal.
abstract: Prior systematic reviews suggest that berberine may match or exceed the effects of metformin on metabolic and hormonal outcomes in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS; previously referred to as polycystic ovary syndrome). This review aimed to assess the reported efficacy of berberine and act as an integrity-based reappraisal of available evidence in women with PMOS. Randomised controlled trials examining berberine supplementation in women with polycystic ovary syndrome were eligible for inclusion. title: Cardiometabolic diseases in transgender populations.

abstract: The number of people seeking gender-affirming medical care and gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) is increasing. As sex steroids shape cardiometabolic physiology, GAHT is expected to meaningfully alter cardiometabolic risk. The aim of this review was to systematically determine and narratively synthesize evidence on the cardiometabolic effects of GAHT and identify clinically relevant knowledge gaps. We searched PubMed for English-language primary human studies published through November 26, 2025. Of 346 screened records, 96 unique original investigations were included. abstract: Diarrheal disease remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality among older adults, yet data on enteric bacterial isolates and antimicrobial resistance in elderly populations in sub-Saharan Africa are limited. abstract: Superior vena cava isolation (SVCI) is performed as an adjunct to pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) for atrial fibrillation, yet whether an empiric or trigger-guided strategy is preferable remains uncertain. abstract: Tiny or very small unruptured intracranial aneurysms (≤3 mm) carry a very low estimated rupture risk, yet many are electively treated. Although factors influencing procedural risks have the potential to guide treatment selection, they remain poorly characterized in this population. titlePt: Molecular and genetic basis of alzheimer's disease and emerging treatment Modalities.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is linked to various causes and pathological processes. It represents a major global health challenge due to its increasing prevalence in aging populations. abstract: Recent trials in BCG-naïve high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (HR-NMIBC) have added immunotherapy to BCG, often using event-free survival (EFS) as the primary endpoint. However, neither EFS nor progression-free survival (PFS) has been validated as a surrogate for overall survival (OS) in this setting. abstract: To characterize the global development, collaboration structure, publication landscape, citation influence and thematic evolution of research on selective GLP-1 receptor agonists and GLP-1-based multi-receptor agonists in T2DM. A bibliometric analysis was conducted on 3736 original articles published between 2004 and 2025 and retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. abstract: This review examines the mechanistic, epidemiological and therapeutic evidence underpinning liver integration into the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) construct. Large cohort data confirm that coexistent metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and CKD confer additive, stage-dependent mortality risk exceeding that of either condition alone, with hepatic fibrosis severity, rather than steatosis, the dominant prognostic driver. abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmia worldwide. Catheter ablation (CA) is an effective therapy for symptomatic AF. title: Updates on paediatric MASLD: insights from an endocrine lens.

abstract: Paediatric metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the leading cause of chronic liver disease in children and adolescents worldwide and is increasing alongside rising rates of paediatric obesity and type 2 diabetes. Paediatric MASLD most often arises in the setting of obesity and metabolic dysfunction but can occur without obesity and is influenced by early life exposures, genetics and environmental factors. abstract: Hypomagnesemia is common in patients with cirrhosis. This retrospective study included patients with cirrhosis who were hospitalized at the First People's Hospital of Changde City, China, between May 2021 and June 2025. abstract: Head and neck cancer (HNC) trials have demonstrated pathological complete response (pCR) in patients receiving neoadjuvant treatment prior to surgery; however, systematic reviews have reported marked variation in pCR rates. abstract: This study investigates the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) as a dynamic marker to track antibiotic efficacy and guide stewardship in term neonates. A retrospective cohort study evaluated 275 term neonates (85 with culture-proven early-onset sepsis [EOS] and 190 controls). Multivariable logistic regression confirmed the independent prognostic value of the SII after adjusting for clinical confounders. abstract: Background/Objective: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), an advanced stage of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), is characterized by progressive liver fibrosis and represents an important therapeutic target. NP-011 is a truncated recombinant human milk fat globule EGF factor 8 protein developed for the treatment of MASH-associated liver fibrosis. Methods: Population pharmacokinetic models were developed using plasma concentration-time data following the intravenous administration of NP-011 in mice, rats, and monkeys. abstract: New cancer medicines increasingly depend on molecular testing, from low-cost immunohistochemistry to expensive genomic diagnostics. The WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (EML) guides access to priority medicines. We aimed to analyse uptake trends for essential cancer medicines in 71 countries and two world regions with lower, middle, and high gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, distinguishing medicines that require immunohistochemistry, complex genomic diagnostics, or neither. titlePt: Durability of pulmonary vein isolation: Does the pulsed field ablation system matter?
abstract: Durable pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is considered the "Achilles' heel" of atrial fibrillation ablation. Although pulsed field ablation (PFA) is increasingly used owing to its nonthermal, tissue-selective properties, comparative data regarding chronic lesion durability across different PFA platforms remain limited. abstract: Direct current cardioversion (DCCV) is commonly performed for atrial fibrillation and flutter (AF/AFL). However, temporal trends and contemporary practices surrounding DCCV are poorly characterized. This study aimed to analyze a large multi-institutional experience of DCCV over 2 decades, quantifying trends, outcomes, and management strategies. For case-level analyses, we identified all DCCVs for AF/AFL between 2000 and 2024 and assessed annual volumes and patient status at the time of DCCV (ie, outpatient, inpatient, or emergency/observation). For patient-level analyses, we focused on individuals who underwent their first (index) DCCV between 2000 and 2022. We evaluated baseline characteristics and outcomes after index DCCV, including AF/AFL recurrence, stroke, heart failure (HF), HF hospitalization, and catheter ablation. abstract: Depressive disorders cause significant global disability, yet oral antidepressants often have systemic side effects and delayed onset. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of facial injections of Botulinum toxin A (BoNT/A) compared with placebo and the active antidepressant sertraline. We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and PsycINFO for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) from inception to December 2025. abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, but their effects on musculoskeletal health remain completely misunderstood. This systematic review/meta-analysis aims to synthesise clinical data on the effects of GLP-1 RAs on key relevant bone, muscle, and joint outcomes. titlePt: The relationship between blood pressure variability, left ventricular hypertrophy, and arterial stiffness in children and adolescents with obesity.
abstract: Obesity and hypertension are major risk factors for cardiovascular target organ damage in childhood, including increased left ventricular mass index (LVMI) and left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). abstract: Anti-amyloid antibodies slow cognitive and functional decline in individuals with early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease, but few studies have examined changes associated with these treatments in plasma biomarkers linked to neurodegeneration. abstract: Endothelial injury is central to sepsis, and altered copper homeostasis may be involved in inflammatory and oxidative stress responses. This study examined the association between plasma copper (Cu) concentrations, endothelial injury markers, inflammatory burden, illness severity, and 28-day mortality in patients with sepsis. This prospective observational study enrolled 100 ICU patients with sepsis between March and December 2025. Patients were classified as survivors or non-survivors according to 28-day outcomes. Correlation, logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), and sensitivity analyses were performed. title: Clinical Diagnosis and Treatment of Anxiety in Dementia With Lewy Bodies.
titlePt: Clinical Diagnosis and Treatment of Anxiety in Dementia With Lewy Bodies.
abstract: Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) is one of the most common neurodegenerative causes of Major Neurocognitive Disorder and associated with a high comorbidity of mood and behavioral disturbances. There is overlap between the defining characteristics of this disorder and the DSM-5-TR criteria for generalized anxiety disorder. DLB causes progressive decline in cognition, motor independence, sleep quality, and mood. Anxiety is the most common mood disturbance in patients with DLB, and those with anxiety experience more frequent and severe cognitive fluctuations. The treatment of underlying anxiety can improve patient and caregiver quality of life, yet screening for anxiety among those with DLB presents unique challenges. This clinical review discusses the importance of screening for anxiety and proposed management of anxiety in patients with DLB. abstract: Women experience more pronounced lipidomic changes with aging than men, which may contribute to the higher rates of Alzheimer's disease seen in postmenopausal women. abstract: Children with Ewing sarcoma (ES) and rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) across Asia, the Middle East and Africa often require cross-border referral for advanced radiotherapy, risking a disruption of multimodality care. abstract: Low-value practices are interventions that do not provide health benefits due to lack of effectiveness or associated risks that outweigh the potential benefits. The purpose of this study is to demonstrate discrepancies across various cardiovascular prevention guidelines published by numerous institutions and organisations, and establish an objective overview of the current state of the art and formulate recommendations for general practitioners. abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is a prevalent chronic liver condition with limited approved pharmacotherapies. abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) (formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome) is a metabolic-endocrine disorder that affects 8-13% of women globally and is associated with increased cardiovascular disease (CVD) across the lifespan. CVD develops in young women due to risk factors such as atherogenic dyslipidaemia, insulin resistance and elevated body weight. title: Integrated omics-driven discovery reveals synphilin-1-mediated anoikis resistance through p53 down-regulation.
titlePt: Integrated omics-driven discovery reveals synphilin-1-mediated anoikis resistance through p53 down-regulation.
abstract: Synphilin-1 is a protein that interacts with α-synuclein and has been implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD). However, the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the effect of synphilin-1 in PD remain poorly understood. The present study aimed to elucidate the molecular function of synphilin-1 using integrated transcriptomic and proteomic in silico analyses, followed by in vitro validation. Synphilin-1 overexpression enhanced cell viability and attenuated pathways associated with cell death. Among the identified regulatory molecules, p53 emerged as a key mediator linking synphilin-1 to suppression of anoikis. Notably, p53 expression demonstrated predominant nuclear localisation in midbrain tissues of individuals with PD. These findings suggest that synphilin-1 promotes cell survival by suppressing p53-mediated anoikis. This regulatory relationship could be crucial for understanding neuroprotective or pathological mechanisms in PD.

title: Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer: Clinical and Molecular Features with Emerging Insights from Comprehensive Genomic Profiling.
titlePt: Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer: Clinical and Molecular Features with Emerging Insights from Comprehensive Genomic Profiling.
abstract: Early‑onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC), defined as colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnosed before 50 years of age, is increasing globally. Colorectal cancer is currently the third most commonly diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, with GLOBOCAN 2024 estimating approximately 2.04 million new cases and 917,895 deaths in 2024. Recent studies indicate a sustained rise in EOCRC incidence across multiple regions and birth cohorts, with the greatest increases observed among younger adults. Although hereditary cancer syndromes account for 20-25% of EOCRC cases, most occur in the absence of known genetic predispositions or established risk factors. title: Effects of Nonsurgical Periodontal Treatment on Salivary Adipokines: A Systematic Review.
titlePt: Effects of Nonsurgical Periodontal Treatment on Salivary Adipokines: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease contributing to systemic metabolic imbalances. Adipose tissue functions as an endocrine organ, releasing adipokines that influence insulin resistance and energy homeostasis. These mediators, such as visfatin, leptin, or adiponectin, may be modulated by periodontal inflammation. This review aims to synthesize current evidence on salivary adipokine levels in periodontitis and to assess the impact of nonsurgical periodontal treatment (NSPT) on these biomarkers. A systematic review was conducted across PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science (April 2025), following PRISMA guidelines. Studies were included if they assessed salivary levels of adipokines (visfatin, adiponectin, leptin, vaspin, adipsin, resistin) before and after NSPT in periodontitis patients. abstract: The prognostic value of red blood cell distribution width (RDW) and the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) in older adults with sepsis remains uncertain. We evaluated their associations with mortality and incremental value beyond clinical predictors. abstract: The early identification of septic patients at high risk of mortality is essential for improving clinical outcomes. abstract: Idiopathic premature adrenarche (IPA) has been associated with a higher risk of metabolic and reproductive dysfunction, but long-term/adult outcomes remain incompletely known. To assess the relationship between IPA and metabolic syndrome, as well as polycystic ovarian syndrome, in premenarcheal adolescent and adult women. abstract: Pediatric arterial ischemic stroke (AIS) is increasing in prevalence, and evidence suggests survivors have a high risk of developing psychiatric conditions, including depression, anxiety, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. Heterogeneous study designs and outcome measures limit comparability. We aimed to systematically review current evidence on prevalence, diagnostic approaches, and treatment of psychiatric conditions after childhood AIS. PubMed and Embase were used to identify studies published between January 2000 and November 2025 evaluating psychiatric outcomes after childhood AIS. Demographic characteristics, stroke features, psychiatric diagnoses, assessment methods, and reported treatments were extracted. abstract: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) imposes a significant clinical burden on patients and a major economic burden on healthcare systems. In HFrEF, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) constitute a cornerstone of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), reducing both mortality and hospitalization. Their use in practice remains suboptimal, largely because of physicians' concerns about adverse events, particularly hyperkalaemia, which may deprive eligible patients of benefit. Only the steroidal MRAs spironolactone and eplerenone are approved for HFrEF, and this consensus document is restricted to these agents. We summarize contemporary evidence across multiple domains related to MRA therapy in HFrEF, including pharmacoepidemiology, the role of biomarkers in predicting outcomes and response to MRA, the pathological role of aldosterone, and the pharmacology and clinical efficacy of steroidal MRAs. abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most common endocrine disorders in women of reproductive age and is associated with infertility, obesity, insulin resistance, and elevated long-term to cardiovascular risk. Traditional diagnostics rely on biochemical examinations and pelvic ultrasonography imaging. These are resource-intensive, operator-dependent, and frequently inaccessible in low-resource settings. Given the pronounced heterogeneity of PCOS phenotypes, traditional single-modality diagnostics frequently fail, necessitating a shift toward multimodal diagnostic approaches. title: Timing of anticoagulation after emergency endovascular therapy for acute ischaemic stroke with atrial fibrillation (TIMERS): protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
titlePt: Timing of anticoagulation after emergency endovascular therapy for acute ischaemic stroke with atrial fibrillation (TIMERS): protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
abstract: The optimal timing for direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) initiation after acute ischaemic stroke in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains unclear, particularly in those undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), who are at higher risk of both haemorrhagic transformation and early embolic recurrence. Patients undergoing thrombectomy have been under-represented in previous randomised trials, resulting in limited evidence for guiding management in this high-risk population. The TIMERS trial aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of early versus delayed initiation of DOACs therapy after EVT in patients with large vessel occlusion stroke and AF. This is a multicentre, prospective, randomised, open-label trial with a blinded outcome assessment. abstract: Plasma tau phosphorylated at threonine 217 (p-tau217), a biomarker of Alzheimer's disease neuropathological changes, can increase before overt symptoms occur. abstract: This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of next-generation immunomodulatory adjuvants (NIAs) and advanced immune characterisation research from 2006 to 2025, aiming to delineate the global landscape, thematic structure, and emerging frontiers in adjuvant immunology. A total of 8637 unique publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus were analysed using bibliometric, network, and co-occurrence approaches. The results show a sharp surge in research output since 2020, driven by mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine development, with the United States and China emerging as dual global research hubs. abstract: Carotid artery web is a rare and underrecognized cause of ischemic stroke. abstract: Observational studies suggest that metabolic/bariatric surgery (MBS) reduces mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with obesity, but adequately powered randomized trials (RCTs) are lacking. abstract: Semaglutide 2·4 mg is a GLP-1 receptor agonist that reduces bodyweight, and provides other cardiometabolic benefits, among people with a BMI at least 30 kg/m2 or at least 27 kg/m2 and with weight-related comorbidities. abstract: Sodium ion (Na⁺), the predominant cation in the extracellular space, is essential for maintaining fundamental cellular activities via preservation of the transmembrane Na⁺ gradient. abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases have traditionally been classified by their predominant protein pathology. However, accumulating evidence reveals extensive molecular cross-talk between distinct pathological proteins, particularly in Alzheimer's disease (AD). abstract: Second-hand smoke (SHS) exposure remains a major source of morbidity and mortality among non-smokers. This study presents the first dedicated Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) publication to systematically quantify SHS prevalence and evaluate its effect as a global risk factor across a broader range of outcomes. Relative risks for nine health outcomes, now including asthma, were estimated using the Burden of Proof methodology, and applied to calculate attributable deaths and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs). title: Infections in Patients with Solid Tumors Undergoing Adoptive Cellular Therapy.
titlePt: Infections in Patients with Solid Tumors Undergoing Adoptive Cellular Therapy.
abstract: Adoptive cellular therapy (ACT) is an increasingly widely used treatment approach for malignancy. While infectious complications of ACT have been well described in patients with hematologic malignancies, limited data are available on the epidemiology of infections in patients with solid tumors. O estudo qualitativo recentemente publicado na *PubMed* (DOI: 10.1080/21645515.2026.2721105) investigou os fatores que influenciam a adesão à vacinação contra o papilomavírus humano (HPV) no Paquistão, um país onde a cobertura vacinal enfrenta desafios estruturais e culturais. Pesquisadores realizaram entrevistas e grupos focais entre fevereiro e agosto de 2025 em distritos do norte e sul de Punjab, incluindo atores-chave como profissionais de saúde, líderes religiosos, educadores, adolescentes e seus responsáveis. Os achados preliminares destacam que a fragilidade do sistema de saúde, restrições financeiras e valores socioculturais complexos atuam tanto como barreiras quanto como facilitadores na implementação da vacina, dependendo do contexto local.

Entre os principais obstáculos identificados estão a desinformação sobre a segurança e eficácia da vacina, a relutância em vacinar adolescentes devido a crenças sobre sexualidade, e a falta de infraestrutura logística para distribuição em áreas rurais. Por outro lado, a participação de líderes comunitários e religiosos mostrou-se crucial para aumentar a confiança, enquanto programas educativos nas escolas foram apontados como estratégias promissoras para engajar jovens e famílias. O estudo não reportou dados quantitativos sobre taxas de cobertura vacinal, mas enfatiza a necessidade de políticas públicas que integrem abordagens culturais sensíveis e investimentos em sistemas de saúde resilientes.

As limitações incluem o caráter qualitativo da pesquisa, que não permite generalizações, e a ausência de informações sobre o impacto de campanhas governamentais prévias. Como próximos passos, os autores sugerem a realização de estudos longitudinais para avaliar a eficácia de intervenções específicas, além de parcerias com organizações não governamentais para ampliar o alcance da vacinação. Para o Paquistão, que planeja o lançamento nacional da vacina contra o HPV, os resultados reforçam a importância de estratégias adaptadas às realidades locais, combinando educação, confiança comunitária e fortalecimento da atenção primária.

---

**English version**

A qualitative study published in *PubMed* (DOI: 10.1080/21645515.2026.2721105) examined the factors influencing human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine uptake in Pakistan, a country grappling with structural and cultural barriers to immunization. Conducted between February and August 2025 across districts in Northern and Southern Punjab, the research engaged diverse stakeholders—healthcare providers, religious scholars, educators, adolescent girls, and their parents/guardians—through interviews and focus groups. Preliminary findings indicate that health system fragility, financial constraints, and sociocultural norms act as both barriers and facilitators, varying by local context.

Key challenges include misinformation about vaccine safety and efficacy, resistance to vaccinating adolescents due to beliefs about sexuality, and logistical gaps in rural distribution. Conversely, the involvement of community and religious leaders emerged as a critical trust-building factor, while school-based education programs were identified as promising strategies to engage youth and families. The study did not report quantitative coverage data but underscores the need for culturally sensitive public policies and resilient health systems.

Limitations include the qualitative nature of the research, which precludes broader generalizations, and the lack of information on prior government campaign impacts. Moving forward, the authors recommend longitudinal studies to assess the effectiveness of targeted interventions, alongside partnerships with nongovernmental organizations to expand vaccine reach. For Pakistan, which is preparing for the national rollout of the HPV vaccine, the findings highlight the necessity of tailored strategies that integrate education, community trust, and primary care strengthening.

title: Nintedanib in the prevention of radiation-induced lung injury in patients with unresectable stage II-III NSCLC: A protocol for a randomized, multicenter, control group study.

abstract: Radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) is a common and dose-limiting complication in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) receiving radiotherapy, especially in combination with chemotherapy and/or immunotherapy. RILI encompasses acute radiation pneumonitis (RP) and chronic pulmonary fibrosis, significantly impacting patients' quality of life and treatment outcomes. Preclinical and clinical evidence suggests that nintedanib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor approved for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), may have preventive effects against RILI due to shared fibrotic pathways. However, prospective data on its prophylactic use remain limited. This is a randomized, multicenter, unblinded, controlled trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of nintedanib in preventing RILI. A total of 66 patients with unresectable stage II-III NSCLC scheduled to receive CCRT will be enrolled from three centers in China. Eligible participants will be randomized 1:1 to either the nintedanib
journalisticSummary:
**Versão em português brasileiro**

Um estudo recente delineia um ensaio clínico pioneiro para avaliar o potencial do nintedanibe na prevenção da lesão pulmonar induzida por radiação (LPIR) em pacientes com câncer de pulmão não pequenas células (CPNPC) em estágios II-III irressecáveis. Publicado na *PLOS ONE*, o protocolo randomizado, multicêntrico e não cego busca recrutar 66 participantes em três centros na China, submetidos a quimiorradioterapia concomitante (QRTc). A LPIR, que inclui pneumonite por radiação aguda e fibrose pulmonar crônica, representa um efeito colateral limitante da radioterapia, agravando a morbidade e comprometendo a continuidade do tratamento oncológico.

O nintedanibe, um inibidor de tirosina quinase já aprovado para fibrose pulmonar idiopática (FPI), atua inibindo múltiplas vias fibróticas, como PDGFR, FGFR e VEGFR. Estudos pré-clínicos sugerem que sua ação anti-fibrótica poderia modular a resposta inflamatória e cicatricial desencadeada pela radiação. No entanto, até o momento, não há dados prospectivos robustos que comprovem sua eficácia profilática contra a LPIR em pacientes com CPNPC. O ensaio, com duração prevista para acompanhar os desfechos por até 12 meses após o término da radioterapia, dividirá os participantes igualmente entre o grupo que receberá nintedanibe (150 mg, duas vezes ao dia) e o grupo controle, que não receberá o fármaco.

Os desfechos primários incluem a incidência e gravidade da pneumonite por radiação, avaliada por critérios clínicos e de imagem (TC de tórax), enquanto os secundários contemplam a progressão para fibrose pulmonar, função respiratória (espirometria) e toxicidade relacionada ao tratamento. Embora os resultados possam abrir caminho para uma estratégia farmacológica adjuvante na radioterapia torácica, o estudo apresenta limitações inerentes ao desenho não cego e ao número reduzido de participantes, o que pode restringir a generalização dos achados. Além disso, não foram informadas nos dados disponíveis as doses exatas de radiação ou regimes quimioterápicos empregados, fatores que influenciam diretamente a incidência de LPIR.

Os próximos passos incluem a conclusão do recrutamento e a análise dos dados, cujos resultados poderão definir se o nintedanibe se tornará uma opção terapêutica para mitigar um dos principais desafios da radioterapia em câncer de pulmão. Caso positivo, o estudo reforçaria a hipótese de que alvos fibróticos compartilhados entre doenças distintas, como a FPI e a LPIR, possam ser explorados clinicamente para melhorar a qualidade de vida de pacientes oncológicos.

---

**English version**

A recent study outlines a groundbreaking clinical trial to assess the potential of nintedanib in preventing radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) in patients with unresectable stage II-III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Published in *PLOS ONE*, the randomized, multicenter, unblinded protocol aims to enroll 66 participants across three centers in China undergoing concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT). RILI, which includes acute radiation pneumonitis and chronic pulmonary fibrosis, remains a dose-limiting complication of radiotherapy, exacerbating morbidity and disrupting oncological treatment continuity.

Nintedanib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor already approved for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), targets multiple fibrotic pathways, including PDGFR, FGFR, and VEGFR. Preclinical studies suggest its anti-fibrotic action may modulate the inflammatory and scarring responses triggered by radiation. However, robust prospective data on its prophylactic efficacy against RILI in NSCLC patients remain scarce. The trial, with an expected follow-up of up to 12 months post-radiotherapy, will randomly assign participants equally to receive nintedanib (150 mg twice daily) or no intervention.

Primary endpoints include the incidence and severity of radiation pneumonitis, assessed through clinical criteria and imaging (chest CT), while secondary outcomes cover progression to pulmonary fibrosis, respiratory function (spirometry), and treatment-related toxicity. While findings could pave the way for an adjunctive pharmacological strategy in thoracic radiotherapy, the study’s unblinded design and limited sample size may constrain the generalizability of results. Additionally, specific radiation doses or chemotherapy regimens were not disclosed in the available data—critical factors influencing RILI incidence.

Next steps involve completing enrollment and data analysis, with results poised to determine whether nintedanib could become a therapeutic option to mitigate one of radiotherapy’s key challenges in lung cancer. If successful, the study would reinforce the hypothesis that shared fibrotic targets across distinct diseases, such as IPF and RILI, may be clinically exploited to improve quality of life in oncology patients.

**Versão em português brasileiro**

Um estudo recente publicado no *Diabetologia* destaca o potencial dos escores pFIB (pFIB-c e pFIB-6), originalmente desenvolvidos para estratificar o risco de fibrose hepática em crianças com doença hepática gordurosa associada à disfunção metabólica (MASLD), como ferramentas promissoras na identificação precoce de crianças obesas com maior probabilidade de desenvolver diabetes tipo 2 de início na juventude. A pesquisa, conduzida por meio do Swedish Childhood Obesity Treatment Register (BORIS, 2005-2020) em parceria com registros nacionais, analisou uma coorte de 4.856 crianças obesas (idade média de 12 anos no início do estudo) e 23.758 comparadores da população geral.

Os resultados indicam que 12,4% das crianças obesas apresentavam um escore pFIB-6 ≥4, um limiar associado a um risco aumentado de diabetes tipo 2. Análises de tempo até o evento, utilizando modelos de regressão de Cox e de sobrevivência paramétrica flexível, revelaram que escores elevados de pFIB-6 estavam significativamente associados a um maior risco de incidência da doença, mesmo após ajustes para fatores de confusão como idade, sexo e índice de massa corporal (IMC). Embora o estudo não tenha detalhado a magnitude exata dos *hazard ratios* (HR), os autores sugerem que a ferramenta pode auxiliar clínicos na priorização de intervenções precoces, como mudanças no estilo de vida ou terapias direcionadas, em subgrupos de alto risco.

Apesar do avanço, os pesquisadores destacam limitações importantes. O estudo baseou-se em dados observacionais, o que impede a inferência de causalidade, e a generalização dos resultados pode ser limitada pela população sueca, predominantemente de origem europeia. Além disso, não foram fornecidos dados sobre a performance discriminativa dos escores (por exemplo, área sob a curva ROC) ou a comparação com outros biomarcadores já estabelecidos, como a hemoglobina glicada (HbA1c). Os próximos passos incluem validações em coortes diversificadas e a avaliação da integração do pFIB-6 em protocolos clínicos de triagem para diabetes tipo 2 em crianças obesas.

---

**English version**

A recent study published in *Diabetologia* explores the potential of the paediatric liver fibrosis risk scores (pFIB-c and pFIB-6), originally designed to stratify fibrosis risk in children with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), as early indicators of type 2 diabetes risk in youth with obesity. Conducted using data from the Swedish Childhood Obesity Treatment Register (BORIS, 2005–2020) linked with national health records, the cohort study analyzed 4,856 children with obesity (mean age 12 years at baseline) and 23,758 general population comparators.

The findings show that 12.4% of children with obesity had a pFIB-6 score ≥4, a threshold associated with an elevated risk of developing youth-onset type 2 diabetes. Time-to-event analyses using Cox regression and flexible parametric survival models demonstrated that higher pFIB-6 scores were significantly associated with an increased risk of incident diabetes, even after adjusting for confounders such as age, sex, and body mass index (BMI). While the study did not specify the exact hazard ratios (HRs), the authors suggest that the score could help clinicians prioritize early interventions—such as lifestyle modifications or targeted therapies—in high-risk subgroups.

However, key limitations must be considered. As an observational study, causal inferences cannot be drawn, and the generalizability of results may be constrained by the Swedish cohort, which is predominantly of European descent. Additionally, the study did not report the discriminative performance of the scores (e.g., area under the ROC curve) or compare them with established biomarkers like glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c). Future research should focus on validating the findings in diverse populations and assessing the integration of pFIB-6 into clinical screening protocols for youth-onset type 2 diabetes in children with obesity.
