A recent study published in PubMed investigated the impact of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1) on postoperative outcomes in patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Obesity and diabetes are risk factors for developing osteoarthritis and are associated with worse outcomes following these surgical procedures. GLP-1 agonists are known to improve glycemic control and promote weight loss. The aim of this study was to assess the effect of GLP-1 treatment on 90-day surgical complications following THA and TKA.

The systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and included studies that reported at least one outcome of interest following primary THA or TKA. In all the studies included, a GLP-1 agonist was prescribed for the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus or for weight loss in obese patients. The primary outcome was the 90-day surgical complication rate in the combined THA and TKA cohort. The 90-day surgical complications were defined as periprosthetic joint infection, wound dehiscence, periprosthetic fracture, hematoma, nerve injury, or surgical site infection.

The main findings indicated that GLP-1 treatment was associated with improved 90-day outcomes after THA and TKA. However, specific details about the magnitude of these effects or how they varied between the different studies included were not provided. The clinical impact of this association suggests that the use of GLP-1 agonists may be beneficial for patients with diabetes or obesity who are scheduled for these surgical procedures, potentially reducing the risk of postoperative complications.

The limitations of the study include the reliance on data from pre-existing studies, which may introduce heterogeneity and bias. Additionally, it was not reported whether the included studies controlled for other factors that could influence the outcomes, such as the presence of comorbidities or the use of other medications. Future steps could include conducting randomized clinical trials to confirm these findings and further explore the mechanisms by which GLP-1 agonists exert their beneficial effects in patients undergoing THA and TKA.

title: Examining the immune response of participants receiving Modified Vaccinia Ankara vaccine in Africa (MpoxVax AFRIVAC): a prospective cohort study - protocol.
titlePt: Examining the immune response of participants receiving Modified Vaccinia Ankara vaccine in Africa (MpoxVax AFRIVAC): a prospective cohort study - protocol.
abstract: Mpox remains an ongoing global health concern, driven by an ongoing clade I outbreak in Central Africa, which has caused substantial morbidity and mortality. Despite deployment of the Modified Vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) vaccine, data on the durability of vaccine-induced immune responses remain limited, particularly in African populations, women and people with HIV, highlighting the need for context-specific immunogenicity data. journalisticSummary:
A doença do vírus mpox continua sendo uma preocupação global de saúde, impulsionada por um surto contínuo da clade I na África Central, que causou morbidade e mortalidade significativas. Apesar do desdobramento da vacina Modified Vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN), os dados sobre a duração das respostas imunológicas induzidas pela vacina permanecem limitados, particularmente em populações africanas, mulheres e pessoas com HIV, destacando a necessidade de dados de imunogenicidade específicos do contexto. O estudo Mpox-Vax AFRIVAC é um estudo de coorte prospectivo e multicêntrico realizado em Uganda, Tanzânia e República Democrática do Congo (RDC). Adultos elegíveis para vacinação com MVA-BN para prevenção de mpox ou que receberam uma primeira dose dentro de 28 dias antes do recrutamento são acompanhados por 48 semanas. Amostras de sangue seriadas são coletadas para quantificar as respostas de anticorpos de ligação e avaliar sua duração ao longo do tempo. Os principais resultados são os títulos médios geométricos de anticorpos específicos para MVA-BN na semana 48 e a taxa de declínio de anticorpos da semana 6 à semana 48.

Os achados principais deste estudo ainda não foram divulgados, pois o resumo apresentado se refere ao protocolo do estudo. No entanto, é esperado que os resultados forneçam informações valiosas sobre a duração da resposta imunológica induzida pela vacina MVA-BN em populações africanas, incluindo subgrupos como mulheres e pessoas com HIV. Esses dados são cruciais para informar estratégias de vacinação eficazes e garantir a proteção contínua contra a doença mpox. As limitações do estudo incluem a falta de informações sobre os resultados clínicos e a possibilidade de viés de seleção de participantes. Os próximos passos incluem a conclusão do estudo e a publicação dos resultados, que devem fornecer insights importantes para a comunidade científica e os formuladores de políticas de saúde.

A colaboração internacional e a pesquisa científica são fundamentais para desenvolver estratégias eficazes de prevenção e tratamento, especialmente em regiões afetadas pela doença.

The mpox virus disease remains an ongoing global health concern, driven by a continuing clade I outbreak in Central Africa, which has caused significant morbidity and mortality. Despite the deployment of the Modified Vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) vaccine, data on the durability of vaccine-induced immune responses remain limited, particularly in African populations, women, and people with HIV, highlighting the need for context-specific immunogenicity data. The Mpox-Vax AFRIVAC study is a prospective, multicenter observational cohort study conducted in Uganda, Tanzania, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Adults eligible for MVA-BN vaccination for mpox prevention or who received a first dose within 28 days prior to enrollment are followed for 48 weeks. Serial blood samples are collected to quantify binding antibody responses and assess their durability over time. The primary outcomes are the mean geometric MVA-BN-specific antibody titers at week 48 and the rate of antibody decay from week 6 to week 48.

The main findings of this study have not been released yet, as the presented abstract refers to the study protocol. However, it is expected that the results will provide valuable information about the duration of the immune response induced by the MVA-BN vaccine in African populations, including subgroups such as women and people with HIV. This data is crucial to inform effective vaccination strategies and ensure continued protection against mpox disease. The limitations of the study include the lack of information on clinical outcomes and the possibility of selection bias of participants. The next steps include completing the study and publishing the results, which should provide important insights for the scientific community and health policymakers.

The mpox virus disease is an ongoing challenge for global health, and studies like Mpox-Vax AFRIVAC are essential to advance knowledge about disease prevention and control. International collaboration and scientific research are fundamental to developing effective prevention and treatment strategies, especially in regions affected by the disease.

titlePt: Emerging biomarkers in breast fibroadenoma: implications for differential diagnosis, malignant transformation, and precision medicine.

journalisticSummary:
O fibroadenoma é a lesão fibroepitelial benigna mais comum da mama, ocorrendo com maior frequência em adolescentes e mulheres em idade reprodutiva. Embora seja considerado uma lesão não invasiva com um bom prognóstico, alguns fibroadenomas podem apresentar crescimento rápido, recorrência, hipercelularidade estromal, alterações proliferativas epiteliais e até mesmo sobreposição radiológica com tumor de phyllodes e carcinoma de mama, resultando em dilemas diagnósticos significativos. Nos últimos anos, estudos de patologia molecular e biomarcadores têm levado a uma melhor compreensão da biologia dos fibroadenomas e sua capacidade de diferenciar entre fibroadenomas e lesões malignas de mama. Essa revisão fornece uma visão geral abrangente dos biomarcadores envolvidos no diagnóstico, prognóstico, previsão, molecular, genético, epigenético, funcional, circulante e de imagem do fibroadenoma de mama e do câncer de mama. Os principais biomarcadores, como a mutação MED12, Ki-67, p53, Bcl-2, ER/PR, HER2, VEGF, MMPs e γ-H2AX, são discutidos. Esses biomarcadores têm o potencial de melhorar a precisão do diagnóstico diferencial e a detecção precoce de transformação maligna, além de orientar a medicina de precisão para pacientes com fibroadenoma de mama. No entanto, mais pesquisas são necessárias para validar a utilidade clínica desses biomarcadores e explorar novas abordagens terapêuticas baseadas em evidências. Com a continuidade dos estudos, espera-se que esses avanços melhorem a compreensão e o manejo do fibroadenoma de mama, contribuindo assim para a melhoria da saúde das mulheres.

The fibroadenoma is the most common benign fibroepithelial lesion of the breast, occurring most frequently in adolescents and women of reproductive age. While it is considered a non-invasive lesion with a good prognosis, some fibroadenomas may exhibit rapid growth, recurrence, stromal hypercellularity, epithelial proliferative changes, and even radiological overlap with phyllodes tumor and breast carcinoma, resulting in significant diagnostic dilemmas. In recent years, molecular pathology and biomarker studies have led to a better understanding of the biology of fibroadenomas and their ability to differentiate between fibroadenomas and malignant breast lesions. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the biomarkers involved in the diagnosis, prognosis, prediction, molecular, genetic, epigenetic, functional, circulating, and imaging of breast fibroadenoma and breast cancer. Key biomarkers such as MED12 mutation, Ki-67, p53, Bcl-2, ER/PR, HER2, VEGF, MMPs, and γ-H2AX are discussed. These biomarkers have the potential to improve the accuracy of differential diagnosis and early detection of malignant transformation, as well as guide precision medicine for patients with breast fibroadenoma. However, further research is needed to validate the clinical utility of these biomarkers and explore new evidence-based therapeutic approaches. With the continuation of studies, it is expected that these advances will improve the understanding and management of breast fibroadenoma, thus contributing to the improvement of women's health.

title: Protocol for a cohort study: evaluating the effect of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy on intraoperative remifentanil consumption during IoC2-guided anesthesia in elderly patients with esophageal cancer.
titlePt: Protocol for a cohort study: evaluating the effect of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy on intraoperative remifentanil consumption during IoC2-guided anesthesia in elderly patients with esophageal cancer.
abstract: The influence of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (nICT) on intraoperative opioid consumption during esophagectomy for cancer is not well understood. IoC2 enables real-time antinociceptive depth monitoring. This study assesses nICT's effect on remifentanil requirements in elderly patients using IoC2. This prospective observational cohort study will be conducted at Jiangsu Cancer Hospital. Sixty patients scheduled for esophagectomy will be enrolled. Patients will be divided into the nICT group (n = 30) or the treatment-naive group (n = 30). All patients will receive a standardized anesthetic protocol. The primary outcome is the mean intraoperative remifentanil infusion rate (μg/kg/min).
